newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie bounce points to more consolidation.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie bounce points to more consolidation.

text.p: *AUD recouped some of Friday's losses on options-related bids and buying on crosses, while a rise in CRB helped at margin
*Bounce has not yet repaired chart damage done by breach of $0.7440 and analysts look for sideways consolidation at best
*RBA board meets but pre-empted by last week's rate cut
*Kiwi down as market eases in expectation of weak jobs data
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local currency had inched up to US$0.7405/10 from US$0.7390/95 late Monday and a US$0.7365 low, but remained adrift of Friday's late US$0.7442/47.

On the wide key levels to watch were last week's high of US$0.7505 and the 18-month low of US$0.7310 hit a fortnight ago. Most chart analysts favoured an eventual break of the latter with the dollar's five month-long downtrend culminating in a retreat to the 1995 trough of US$0.7070.
On the topside strong technical resistance was expected at US$0.7530/7550 but some bulls felt US$0.7650 was an attainable target in the medium term.
Some of the New Zealand dollar's wekaness has rubbed off on the A$ recently, so bulls were relieved to see the Kiwi firm this morning after jobs data proved less weak than expected.

The New Zealand unemployment rate edged up to 6.7 percent in June from 6.5 percent but market forecasts had been for a 6.9 percent level. Dealers said there had been speculation a very weak result would have forced the Reserve Bank to sanction a market-led easing, although many felt the bank would probably have to allow some loosening in its tight policy anyway.
The Kiwi rose to US$0.6450 from US$0.6425/30 immediately after the data, but then pulled back to US$0.6433/40.
The A$ held firm at NZ$1.150525 from NZ$1.1476/01.
Australian markets face their own jobs test Thursday amid a lingering suspicion another weak employment result would start the whole rate cut circus once again.

Bulls had hoped last week's 50 basis point easing to 5.00 percent would be the last in the cycle and many analysts thought it probably was. But with the inflation outlook so favourable another could not be ruled out if data continued to disappoint.
The RBA's board meets today but it will be something of a non-event given an impromptu meeting had been held last week to sanction Wednesday's easing. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
